problem: What is the limit of the sequence ${a}_{n}=\frac{-{n}^{3}+10}{3{n}^{2}-n}$ for $n\ge 1?$

feedback.problem: What is the limit of the sequence ${a}_{n}=\frac{1-{n}^{4}}{3{n}^{2}+5}$ for $n\ge 1?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The dominant term  in the denominator is $3{n}^{2}$, so we divide the numerator and the denominator by ${n}^{2}$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{n\to \infty }{a}_{n} & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{1-{n}^{4}}{3{n}^{2}+5} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{1}{{n}^{2}}-\frac{{n}^{4}}{{n}^{2}})}{(\frac{3{n}^{2}}{{n}^{2}}+\frac{5}{{n}^{2}})} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{1}{{n}^{2}}-{n}^{2})}{(3+\frac{5}{{n}^{2}})} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{0-{n}^{2}}{3+0} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }(-\frac{{n}^{2}}{3}) \\  & =-\infty .\end{aligned}
$$

The limit does not exist, so the sequence diverges.
